fig_cmazet_door_then_tint.door_search_rule:
PW-1 item 16.2: n-CLU successes on door transitions, found BY RULE in the persisted per-item scores.

Reads data/cmazet_items.json (base n-CLU, seeds 0-2: the only base seeds with persisted objects)
and data/cmazet_items_rel.json (n-CLU-REL, seeds 0-5). Loads no model; no scoring.

Classes, per model, per seed, over the held-out TEST n-way rows:
  door_open          truth key event > k (a key consumed at a door: the door opens) AND n-CLU correct
  door_then_tint     family == "interaction" (door colour = pocket colour = target tint) AND n-CLU correct
  most_baselines_wrong  n-CLU correct AND >= 4 of the 6 matched baselines wrong
                     (rival: {mlp,lstm,transformer} at 8,000 and 80,000 steps, the run's own objects)
The draw: numpy default_rng(DRAW_SEED), one generator, calls in the fixed order of ALLOCATION.
Within a draw, the qualifying items are grouped into strata (family, colour = pocket colour); the
strata are visited in a random permutation and one item is drawn uniformly inside each stratum, so
consecutive draws differ in family or colour wherever the set allows it. A draw never repeats an item.
An empty class is recorded as empty; nothing is substituted.

fig_cmazet_families.notes: One held-out TEST n-way transition per rule family: the first in the scorer's capped order at seed 0, else at the first seed that has one. Columns: s_t with the action, the engine's s_{t+1}, then each arm's generated s_{t+1} (apply_outcome of its own emission) with the engine's judge's mark. Margin = single design - best learned baseline (mlp_180k, chosen per arm); a DIFFERENT opponent from the ladder's learned 1x, so this figure is never merged with fig_ladder. Equal compute: 400 steps / 25,600 images per arm-run (printed in CROSS-ARM.md).

fig_ladder.notes: PW-1 item 10: one panel, no title, legend at the right. 3 seeds (0, 1, 2) on every rung; line = mean of the three per-seed values, dots = seeds. The one landed rival column set (data/ladder_rival_sets.json; the 32,256-row and the 32,768-row data-matched MLP sets are retired by item 10.1), beside the store (KSTAR-LADDER.json by_rung.*.kstar_K32.store; asserted equal, seed by seed, to SHAPES-MATCHED.json ladder.*.arms.store_K32_n131072) and table floor. Pool size and optimiser steps are asserted from the artefact and printed in the caption. Set drawn: data_matched_131072: Data-matched rivals, 131,072-row pool, 131,072 rows, 20,480/204,800 steps (each rung's own 131,072-row pool, the store's exact rows; P1-carried fit per family and seed); source w20-shapes-data-matched/SHAPES-MATCHED.json. w20 set: the P1-carried fit per family and seed (P3_margin.store_K32_n131072.per_family.*.*.carried_rival); a filled dot is a seed carried at its 204,800-step (10x) fit, an open dot the 20,480-step fit. For n >= 3 the rungs probe the identical 120 corners.

fig_maze_conditions.notes: PW-1 item 1. (a) four input conditions, primary row unseen n-way (the engine's judge); every seed a row has is drawn (3 for the words-full and observation rows, from their BARS artefacts; 6 for the two words-plus-observation rows, from each seed's run JSON via maze_six.py, asserted float-equal to REL-NEWSEEDS.json). Comparator = the matched baseline with the highest mean over the row's seeds (every kind, both step limits); for the n-CLU-REL row, Transformer-REL at the step limit with the higher six-seed mean. (b), (c) per seed: n-CLU / n-CLU-REL, the (a) comparator of that row, and the highest control (max over the four controls on that seed). No claim label, no ceiling, no hard/easy class, no text over the data.

a.rule:
RULE (written after seeing only the bank's FIRST maze, never the chosen one): walk the seed-0 TRAIN bank's generator sequence exactly
    as ``build_bank`` does (base 2_000_000, rng seed base + 5551, ``tinted_door_instance``); take
    the FIRST maze whose optimal route picks up >= 2 keys; show the state right after its
    second pickup (one door already opened, one key in the pocket).
